The concept of punishment has to be kept apart from its justification because whether and how punishment can be justified depends on the concept we employ. If we define punishment loosely, or already assume it is justified, we can't ask the critical question of whether it is justified at all. Defining it first gives us a neutral object whose justification, whether retributive, deterrent or rehabilitative, can then be tested.
